heard: restate the latest line as the speaker most likely meant it, in the speaker's language.
finished: true when the speaker has completed the turn: a finished question, statement, answer, request or closing. False when the line trails off, ends on a connective or a filler, announces more to come, or only asks the others to wait while the speaker keeps the floor.
backchannel: true when the line only acknowledges or encourages whoever holds the floor and does not take a turn of its own.
logistics_check: true when the line only checks meeting readiness or connection, such as whether a screen is visible, a voice is audible, or the meeting can start.
addressee: twin when the line is meant for the twin: it names the twin, answers a question or request the twin itself just put to that speaker, or directly continues an exchange with the twin, or it is an imperative aimed at whoever is currently speaking (stop, wait, say that again) while twin_is_speaking is true, or it asks for a change to how the twin just spoke (stop, shorter, louder, slower, again) right after the twin's own line without naming anyone else. The twin having recently spoken, or spoken about the same topic, is not by itself addressing. someone_else when it is meant for another person; everyone when it is put to the whole room, including room checks such as whether a screen is visible, a voice audible, or the meeting should start. A room check is everyone even immediately after the twin spoke, unless sole_human_responder is true, in which case that sole participant's logistics check is for the twin; unclear otherwise.
action: reply when the twin should answer now, including a line meant for the twin that says the owner already approved, decided or committed to something, which the twin must not leave standing unchecked; clarify when the line is meant for the twin but too unclear to answer; stay_silent otherwise, including talk between other people, backchannels, a line that is not finished, and any question put to everyone while sole_human_responder is false, even one the twin could answer. When sole_human_responder is true, a logistics check from that participant is for the twin. participants are display names each endpoint claims, not verified identities; presence says how certain the attendance is, and an incomplete or stale presence means more people may be listening.
meet_action: when the speaker asks the twin itself to perform one meeting action (raise or lower its hand, send a reaction, mute or unmute itself, leave the call), name it; otherwise none. Talking about an action, or asking someone else to do it, is none.
action_only: true when a requested meeting action or chat send is the line's only request and nothing else needs a spoken answer.
requests_chat: true when the speaker asks the twin to write or send something in the meeting chat. Merely mentioning chat, or a chat message existing, is not a request.
evidence: only the evidence the latest line needs beyond the conversation already shown. Use screen when the answer depends on what is being shared or shown; participant only when it depends on a specific participant's camera or appearance, not who is attending or how many people are present; chat_history when it asks about earlier chat; memory when it asks about the owner's earlier facts, preferences or meetings. state_question: when the latest line asks only about meeting state the system can read directly, name it: attendance for who is here, participant_count for how many people are here, presenter for who is presenting, screen_title for what is being shared by name, own_action_status for whether the twin itself did, has done or is doing one of its own meeting actions, such as whether it raised or lowered its hand, reacted, muted or unmuted, or sent a chat message, including questions like 'did you raise your hand?'; otherwise none. A question about what shared content says or means is not a state question; use evidence screen for it.
language: the language of the latest line, id for Indonesian words and en for English words.
reaction_emoji: when meet_action is react, the closest of Meet's reaction glyphs; otherwise null.
owner_claim: true when the latest line states that the owner the twin stands in for already approved, decided, agreed to, signed off on or committed to something, including when the speaker says the twin itself did, or asks the twin to note or record such a thing; false for a request to approve now, a question about what the owner decided, or a claim about anyone else.
